name: Baby Purple
lede: Baby Purple is a pale, slightly pink-leaning purple from the xkcd color survey, one of hundreds of crowd names for the pastel end of the purple family.

sections.title: A crowd name, not a dictionary one
sections.body:
Baby Purple comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where hundreds of thousands of visitors typed a name next to a swatch and the most common labels for each cluster of clicks became its name [1]. Who first typed "baby purple" for this particular shade is undocumented: the survey only records which name won, not who wrote it first [1].

The "baby" here works the way it does in [[baby-blue-eyes|baby blue]] and baby pink: a light, washed-out version of the main color, not a reference to any specific object. Our library's closest standard name is [[lavender|Lavender]], about 4 points off in CIEDE2000, and the survey separately recorded a near-identical click cluster as "Pastel Purple," less than 2 units away [1]. Nearby in the family are [[purple]] and [[violet]], both considerably more saturated.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this exact pale purple covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. That is expected: Baby Purple is a 2010s screen color at full saturation and high lightness, well outside what historical pigments and aged varnish produce [2]. Measured values are a computed color match against museum photographs, not a pigment identification [2].
